confirmed.title: Prior-cache write race if training starts before the pilot prebuild finishes
confirmed.detail: nodal_prior_features and the currently-running build_prior_cache process both do an unlocked read-modify-write of the same results/prior_cache/doe_data_v2/case_02xx.npz files, and both use the IDENTICAL tmp path cache_file.with_suffix('.tmp.npz') (prior.py:205). The trainer builds graphs sequentially in its main process (train_doe_curl_mgn.py:593 loop -> prior.py), so the race is exactly trainer-vs-prebuild. If the trainer reaches a pilot case the builder has not finished, it recomputes the missing steps (duplicate ~0.3 s/step solves, adding up to ~20 min launch delay) AND writes the same npz the builder is writing. Two writers on one tmp file: writer A finishes and os.replace()s the tmp while writer B still holds the fd and keeps writing to the same inode -> the renamed-in-place cache file receives interleaved bytes (corrupt zip); B's own os.replace then raises FileNotFoundError, killing that process. Additionally both np.load calls (prior.py:184 read path, prior.py:201 merge path) are unguarded, and on the Docker Desktop Windows mount (gRPC-FUSE) rename atomicity is not POSIX-guaranteed, so a reader can also see a partial file. A corrupt case_02xx.npz raises zipfile.BadZipFile on every subsequent access, so not only does the 32 h launch crash mid-graph-build, every retry crashes at the same case until the file is manually deleted. Prebuild status at audit time: case ~255/320, ~15 s/case, ~15 min remaining (results/logs/prior_cache_v2_build.log). Verified-clean context: legacy cases 0-239 hit the fully-populated doe_data_240 cache dir (240/240 files, absent-cs_=1.0 rule) without recompute -- the builder log shows cases 0-240 passing in ~125 s, i.e. pure hits -- so the race is confined to the 80 pilot files.
confirmed.scenario: run_v2_320_docker.sh is launched while the prebuild is still running. Preflights take a few minutes; the trainer's graph build then walks cases 0..319 and reaches the pilot range while the builder is at, say, case 300. During the overtake window both processes write case_03xx.npz through the same case_03xx.tmp.npz path; one interleaved write lands a corrupt npz in place. The trainer (or a later resume) hits np.load -> BadZipFile ~30-60 min into the launch, uncaught, training dies -- and because the run script does not abort on failure (see the other finding), scoring then proceeds against a stale checkpoint.
confirmed.fix: Operational (sufficient for this launch): do not start run_v2_320_docker.sh until 'PRIOR_CACHE_DONE' appears in results/logs/prior_cache_v2_build.log (~15 min away). Code hardening (2 lines): make the tmp path process-unique, e.g. cache_file.with_suffix(f'.{os.getpid()}.tmp.npz'), and wrap both np.load(cache_file) calls in try/except (BadZipFile, OSError, ValueError) that treats the file as a cache miss and recomputes/overwrites.
confirmed.verify_reason: Defect is real. prior.py:205 uses a process-shared tmp path (cache_file.with_suffix('.tmp.npz'), no PID, no lock) for an unlocked read-modify-write (lines 195-207), and both the running builder (build_prior_cache.py:45) and the trainer (train_doe_curl_mgn.py:604 -> build_curl_graph -> nodal_prior_features at line 230) go through this exact code. The trainer's graph-build loop (train_doe_curl_mgn.py:576-604) iterates ALL 320 records sequentially in the main process before the split is applied (line 676), so it will walk into the pilot range 240-319. The prebuild log shows the builder at case 274/320 (~14 s/case, ~11 min left, no PRIOR_CACHE_DONE), while legacy cases 0-239 are pure cache hits, so a trainer launched now converges on the builder's position and both compute identical steps in lockstep on the same case_02xx.npz — collision probability is high, not theoretical. Two concurrent np.savez_compressed on the identical tmp path plus os.replace produces a corrupt npz and/or FileNotFoundError, and both np.load calls (prior.py:184, 201) are unguarded, so a corrupt file raises BadZipFile on every retry until manually deleted. run_v2_320_docker.sh has no wait on the prebuild. One peripheral correction: the script DOES abort scoring on train failure (lines 78-86), so the 'scoring against a stale checkpoint' tail of the scenario is wrong, but the race, the crash, and the persistent corrupt-cache consequence stand. The proposed operational fix (wait for PRIOR_CACHE_DONE) and code hardening (PID-unique tmp, guarded loads) are correct.

confirmed.title: No gate on prior-cache prebuild completion: launching while the running prebuild is still writing case_02xx.npz can crash training on a tmp-file collision or corrupt a cache entry
confirmed.detail: fem_warmstart/prior.py:195-207 writes each cache entry via read-existing -> np.savez_compressed(case_XXXX.tmp.npz) -> os.replace. The tmp path is deterministic per case, so two processes computing the same uncached pilot case (the prebuild now running — currently at case 255/320, only 18/80 pilot files written under results/prior_cache/doe_data_v2, with case_0251.tmp.npz live on disk — and the training run's dataset build with --prior-features) collide: interleaved savez writes can corrupt the shared tmp before one os.replace promotes it (a corrupt .npz then raises BadZipFile on every later np.load of that case), and the second os.replace raises FileNotFoundError after the first process renames the tmp away, killing the trainer during dataset construction. The script has preflights for the split digest and V3 identity but none for pilot cache completeness.
confirmed.scenario: Operator starts run_v2_320_docker.sh while prior_cache_v2_build is still running (it is running right now); both processes hit case_02xx concurrently; training dies with FileNotFoundError in os.replace during epoch-0 dataset build, or a corrupted case_02xx.npz poisons this and every future --prior-features run of that case.
confirmed.fix: Add a preflight-3 before TRAIN: assert all 80 files results/prior_cache/doe_data_v2/case_0240.npz .. case_0319.npz exist, each np.load-able with step_/cs_ keys for all 45 steps, and that no *.tmp.npz remains in the directory (a leftover tmp implies a writer is active or died mid-write); abort otherwise. Operationally: do not launch until results/logs/prior_cache_v2_build.log reports case 320/320.
confirmed.verify_reason: The defect is real. run_v2_320_docker.sh (lines 35-64) has only two preflights — split digest and V3 byte-identity — and launches train_doe_curl_mgn.py --prior-features at line 68 with no check on prior-cache completeness or leftover *.tmp.npz files. The prebuild is verifiably running concurrently (prior_cache_v2_build.log at case 263/320; case_0264.npz written seconds before inspection; only 25/80 pilot files present), and both the prebuild (fem_warmstart/build_prior_cache.py:45) and the trainer (train_doe_curl_mgn.py:230, cache=True default, PRIOR_CACHE_DISABLE unset) funnel into the identical unguarded writer at fem_warmstart/prior.py:205-207: tmp = cache_file.with_suffix(".tmp.npz"); np.savez_compressed(tmp, ...); os.replace(tmp, cache_file). The tmp name is deterministic per case (case_02xx.tmp.npz), there is no locking or per-process uniquification, and no try/except protects savez, os.replace, or the np.load read path (prior.py:184, 200-202). Two concurrent writers on the same uncached pilot case therefore can (a) raise FileNotFoundError in the loser's os.replace after the winner consumes the shared tmp — killing the trainer during epoch-0 graph construction — or (b) promote a partially written zip when one process's os.replace fires while the other is mid-savez, producing a persistent BadZipFile-poisoned case_02xx.npz that crashes every subsequent --prior-features touch of that case (the recompute path re-reads the corrupt file at prior.py:200-202, so it never self-heals). The per-step read-modify-write pattern (45 write/replace cycles per case on each side) makes the collision window wide. Minor factual drift in the claim (its snapshot said case 255/320, 18/80 files, a live case_0251.tmp.npz; I observed 263/320, 25/80 files, no tmp at that instant) does not affect the mechanism. The proposed preflight-3 (assert all 80 pilot npz files load with step_/cs_ keys for 45 steps and no *.tmp.npz remains, or wait for the prebuild log to reach 320/320) is a correct minimal fix.

confirmed.title: Scoring failures still end in 'V2 320 DONE' -> heartbeat reports a failed run as completed
confirmed.detail: The train step is now exit-gated (line 78-86, added mid-audit), but the eval.benchmark scoring step (lines 88-94) and the grouped-summary heredoc (96-125) are not: their exit codes are echoed and ignored, and line 126 prints 'V2 320 DONE' unconditionally. eval.benchmark deliberately exits 1 when a model scores zero samples (benchmark.py:894-902) precisely because a structurally-complete-but-empty scorecard looks like success; this script swallows that signal. Compounding it, heartbeat.py checks DONE_RE before FAIL_RE (heartbeat.py:132-137), so a log containing both a Traceback and the DONE banner is classified 'completed'.
confirmed.scenario: A systematic scoring fault (e.g. a pilot-case prior rebuild error, or the curl ckpt rejected) makes benchmark exit 1 with n_samples=0 after the 32 h train; the grouped heredoc then KeyErrors on s['by_case'] (summarize() returns only {'n_samples':0,'note':...}), GROUPS exit=1 is echoed, 'V2 320 DONE' prints anyway, and the heartbeat/twice-daily brief reports status=completed. On a retry the heredoc could even summarize a stale benchmark JSON left by a previous attempt (none exists today, but any failed re-run creates one). The section-27 verdict artifact is missing or stale while everything says done.
confirmed.fix: Mirror the TRAIN_EXIT pattern: capture SCORE_EXIT and GROUPS_EXIT, and on nonzero print 'V2 SCORING FAILED' and exit 1 without printing the DONE banner; print 'V2 320 DONE' only when all three exits are 0. Optionally also delete/rename ${SCORE} before the scoring step so a retry can never summarize a stale artifact.
confirmed.verify_reason: The defect is real, confirmed at every link of the chain. (1) run_v2_320_docker.sh runs under `set -u` only (line 25, no `set -e`); the scoring step's exit code is discarded by `echo "SCORE exit=$?"` (line 94), the grouped-summary heredoc's by `echo "GROUPS exit=$?"` (line 125), and line 126 prints "V2 320 DONE" unconditionally — only the train step (lines 78-86) is exit-gated. (2) eval/benchmark.py summarize() lines 272-275 returns {"n_samples": 0, "note": "no samples scored"} with no by_case/overall/torque keys when zero samples score, and main() (~lines 895-903) still writes the scorecard JSON but returns 1 — so a systematic scoring fault yields an on-disk SCORE file that makes the heredoc KeyError at line 104 (s["by_case"]), both failures swallowed, DONE printed anyway. (3) heartbeat.py lines 132-135 check DONE_RE (r"^.*\bDONE\s*$", multiline — matches "V2 320 DONE") before FAIL_RE, so a log containing both a Traceback and the DONE banner is classified log_status="completed", which build_status() (line 144) prefers over the control-file hint; the brief then reports a failed run as completed. The stale-artifact point also holds: nothing removes ${SCORE} before scoring, so a retry can summarize a leftover JSON from a prior failed attempt. Only trivial inaccuracy: the benchmark.py exit block is at ~895-903 rather than 894-902. The proposed fix (capture SCORE_EXIT/GROUPS_EXIT, fail loudly on nonzero, print DONE only when all three are 0, pre-delete ${SCORE}) is correct.

confirmed.title: Reboot recovery: re-running the script as-is clobbers the accumulated checkpoint at epoch 1
confirmed.detail: The train line (68-77) has no --resume plumbing. In train_doe_curl_mgn.py a fresh run starts with best_val=inf, so after epoch 1 it torch.saves over args.ckpt (line 937) and, with --ckpt-every 1, over <ckpt>.last (line 942). The resume hint at line 84 only prints when TRAIN_EXIT!=0 -- after a host reboot the --rm container simply vanishes, nothing prints, and the natural operator move ('just re-run the script') destroys both recovery files within ~40 minutes. Docker restart policies do NOT help and would make this worse: Docker Desktop does not auto-start after a Windows reboot (confirmed in hb_control.json's own note), and an auto-restarted container would re-enter the script WITHOUT --resume and clobber exactly as above. Do not add one; with --ckpt-every 1 a manual resume costs at most 1 epoch (~40 min) plus the ~30-60 min graph build and preflight.
confirmed.scenario: Host reboots at hour 20 (~epoch 28). On disk: results/mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior.pt (best-val so far) and .pt.last (epoch 28). Operator restarts Docker Desktop and re-runs run_v2_320_docker.sh unmodified; at the new run's epoch 1 both files are overwritten with an epoch-1 model and 20 hours are silently gone -- the run 'succeeds' 32 h later having trained 50 fresh epochs, so nothing ever flags it.
confirmed.fix: Add resume plumbing now, before launch: e.g. RESUME="${RESUME:-}" at the top and append ${RESUME:+--resume "${RESUME}"} to the train line. Exact operator recovery after a reboot: (1) start Docker Desktop; (2) relaunch the same docker run (-e PYTHONPATH=/workspace/app -v "D:\KDH\NvidiaNemo:/workspace/app" -w /workspace/app nvcr.io/nvidia/physicsnemo/physicsnemo:26.03) with RESUME=results/mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior.pt.last bash results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh, appending output to results/logs/v2_320.log. Equivalently the bare trainer command is: python -u train_doe_curl_mgn.py --data-dir backup/doe_data_v2 --split eval/splits/doe_v2_case_split.json --target B --no-wrap-rotor --no-anti-periodic-edges --prior-features --model mgn --hidden-dim 256 --processor-size 15 --band-spectral-weight 30 --epochs 50 --batch-size 1 --step-stride 1 --ckpt results/mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior.pt --ckpt-every 1 --resume results/mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior.pt.last (every run-defining flag must match; the drift check refuses otherwise). Then the script's scoring steps run automatically.
confirmed.verify_reason: Defect confirmed by code inspection. run_v2_320_docker.sh lines 68-77 contain no --resume flag and no RESUME env plumbing (only BAND_W/EPOCHS/TAG at lines 27-29 are overridable); CKPT is deterministic from TAG (line 30) so a re-run targets the same files. In train_doe_curl_mgn.py a fresh run initializes best_val=inf (line 758), so after epoch 1 the best-val save at lines 935-937 unconditionally overwrites args.ckpt, and with --ckpt-every 1 (script line 77) lines 941-942 overwrite <ckpt>.last the same epoch. There is no existing-checkpoint guard. The resume hint at script lines 82-85 prints only on TRAIN_EXIT!=0 within a live script run; a host reboot kills the container without triggering it, both preflights pass again on re-run, and the re-run silently destroys both recovery files within one epoch (~40 min). The claimed scenario (reboot at hour 20, unmodified re-run, 20 h of compute lost with no flag) is mechanically accurate. Minimal fix as proposed: RESUME="${RESUME:-}" plus ${RESUME:+--resume "${RESUME}"} on the train line; the trainer already supports --resume with flag-drift refusal (lines 760-800).

refuted.title: Grouped summary crashes: by_case metrics are nested under 'channels'
refuted.reason: The defect does not exist in the current uncommitted script. results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh line 108 reads `bs = [v["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"] for v in rows.values()]` and line 114 reads `rows[k]["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"]` — both already use the nested "channels" level that eval/benchmark.py summarize() (line 293-296) produces for by_case entries ({"n_samples", "channels": {...}, "torque"}). The flat access `v["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"]` quoted in the claim appears nowhere in the file; the auditor's proposed fix is verbatim what the script already contains, so the described KeyError cannot happen.

refuted.title: Script does not abort when training fails — a partial checkpoint gets scored as if final
refuted.reason: The claim misreads the script. In D:\KDH\NvidiaNemo\results\logs\run_v2_320_docker.sh, line 78 is `TRAIN_EXIT=$?` (not a bare `echo "TRAIN exit=$?"`), and lines 80-86 explicitly gate scoring on it: `if [ "${TRAIN_EXIT}" -ne 0 ]; then echo "V2 TRAIN FAILED -- skipping scoring. Resume with:" ... exit 1; fi`, preceded by a comment (lines 80-81) stating a benchmark JSON after a failed train "would poison the section-27 verdict". So if training dies mid-run with a nonzero exit, the script prints TRAIN exit=N, prints the resume instruction referencing ${CKPT}.last, and exits 1 before eval.benchmark (line 89) or the grouped-summary heredoc (line 97) ever run — no scorecard or groups JSON is produced from a partial checkpoint. The exit status is captured correctly: line 78 immediately follows the train command (lines 68-77), so $? is the trainer's status. The auditor's proposed fix is essentially what the script already implements. One residual caveat (outside the claim as stated): the guard only fires on a nonzero exit of the train process; a host power-loss/restart kills the whole script (docker run included), so scoring never runs in that scenario either — there is no path where eval.benchmark scores a partial checkpoint in the same invocation. The only theoretical gap would be a manual re-invocation of just the scoring block after a crash, which is operator action, not a script defect.

refuted.title: Grouped-summary heredoc indexes by_case wrong: KeyError 'Bnorm' kills the section-27 verdict artifact
refuted.reason: The heredoc in results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh already indexes through the "channels" level: line 108 reads v["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"] and line 114 reads rows[k]["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"] — character-for-character identical to the auditor's proposed fix. eval/benchmark.py summarize() (lines 290-300) confirms the per-case entry is {"n_samples", "channels": {...}, "torque": ...}, so these accesses match the artifact structure and no KeyError 'Bnorm' can occur. The auditor evidently reproduced the failure with the unfixed expression against the doe120 artifact, but that expression is not what the script contains. All other heredoc paths the auditor checked (model key, overall/by_region/torque paths, int(ci) group matching) are correct as conceded. Minor separate observation (not the claimed defect): line 109 assumes every per-case entry has a "torque" key, which summarize() only writes when torque samples exist for that case.

refuted.title: Training failure does not stop the script — a partially trained (or on rerun, stale) checkpoint is scored and packaged as the verdict
refuted.reason: The defect does not exist in the file that will run. results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh lines 78-86 already capture the train exit status (TRAIN_EXIT=$?) and abort with exit 1 before any scoring when it is nonzero, printing "V2 TRAIN FAILED -- skipping scoring" plus a --resume hint — i.e. the auditor's own proposed fix is already implemented verbatim, complete with a comment naming the scorecard-poisoning risk. Line 78 is not `echo "TRAIN exit=$?"` as claimed. The rerun scenario also cannot occur: a fresh launch re-executes training (line 68) before the scoring block, so eval.benchmark can only ever score a checkpoint produced by a train call that just returned 0 in the same run; a stale checkpoint from a prior failed attempt is never reachable by the scoring step. The claim was evidently written against an older or imagined version of the script.

refuted.title: Run script scores a stale or partially-trained checkpoint after a training crash
refuted.reason: The defect does not exist in the current run_v2_320_docker.sh. The claim asserts line 78 "merely echoes 'TRAIN exit=$?' and unconditionally proceeds to eval.benchmark". In the actual file, line 78 is TRAIN_EXIT=$? (captured immediately after the train command, lines 68-77), line 79 echoes the saved variable, and lines 82-86 gate scoring exactly as the auditor's proposed fix suggests: if [ "${TRAIN_EXIT}" -ne 0 ] the script prints "V2 TRAIN FAILED -- skipping scoring", suggests a --resume command, and exits 1 before eval.benchmark (line 89) and before the grouped-summary heredoc (line 97). Therefore a crash at epoch 7 (or any nonzero train exit, including one with a stale pre-existing ${CKPT}) produces no benchmark JSON and no _groups.json, so the section-27 verdict cannot silently consume a partially-trained or last-week checkpoint. The auditor evidently reviewed a stale draft; the proposed fix is already implemented verbatim in spirit.

refuted.title: GROUPS heredoc reads by_case[...]["Bnorm"] but metrics are nested under "channels" — KeyError, section-27 artifact never written
refuted.reason: The defect does not exist in the actual file. results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh already accesses the metrics through the "channels" level: line 108 reads `v["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"]` and line 114 reads `rows[k]["channels"]["Bnorm"]["nrmse_pct"]` — exactly the code the claim proposes as the fix. It even already records per-group torque via `v["torque"]["nrmse_torque_pct"]` (lines 109, 113), which is correct because eval/benchmark.py summarize() (lines 293-300) builds each by_case entry as {"n_samples", "channels": {...}, "torque": ...} with torque as a sibling of "channels". The claimed bare `v["Bnorm"]` accesses appear nowhere in the script (grep confirms no such pattern), so the KeyError scenario and the missing groups artifact cannot occur as described. The auditor evidently diffed against a stale/hypothetical version of the heredoc.

refuted.title: No exit-code gate after TRAIN: a mid-run training death still produces a complete, verdict-named score JSON from a partially trained checkpoint
refuted.reason: The claimed defect does not exist in the current script. results/logs/run_v2_320_docker.sh lines 78-86 already implement exactly the gate the auditor says is missing: line 78 captures TRAIN_EXIT=$? immediately after the train command, and lines 82-86 exit 1 with a "V2 TRAIN FAILED -- skipping scoring" message (plus a --resume ${CKPT}.last hint) whenever TRAIN_EXIT != 0. Lines 80-81 even carry a comment naming the exact hazard ("a benchmark JSON produced after a failed train looks exactly like a real scorecard and would poison the section-27 verdict"). Therefore a mid-run training death (e.g. rc=137 at epoch 30) aborts the script before the SCORE block (line 89) and GROUPS block (line 97) run; no verdict-named score JSON can be produced from a partially trained checkpoint. The auditor's description of line ~78 as "followed only by echo TRAIN exit=$?" mismatches the actual file. Minor residue: SCORE's exit code (line 94) is echoed but not gated before GROUPS; however a failed SCORE leaves no ${SCORE} file, so GROUPS raises FileNotFoundError (visible GROUPS exit=1) and writes no _groups.json, and no stale benchmark JSON for TAG doe_v2_bw30_prior exists in results/ to be silently summarized — this is a robustness nit, not the claimed silent-failure path.

minors.title: Prior-cache write race if training launches before the running prebuild finishes
minors.detail: nodal_prior_features writes via a FIXED temp name: tmp = cache_file.with_suffix('.tmp.npz') then os.replace(tmp, cache_file). The prebuild (results/logs/prior_cache_v2_build.log, at case 266/320 when observed, ~14 s/case, ~13 min to finish) and a concurrently launched training/eval process that finds a step missing in the same case_02xx.npz will both open the same .tmp.npz. On the Windows-mounted volume, os.replace on a file another process holds open raises PermissionError, and interleaved writes can leave a corrupt npz at the final path that a later np.load raises BadZipFile on — killing the graph-build hours in.

minors.title: Non-atomic torch.save can corrupt the best-val checkpoint on a crash mid-write
minors.detail: torch.save(checkpoint_payload(ep), args.ckpt) at line 937 (and the .last save at 942) writes directly to the final path. A ~110 MB payload takes seconds on the mounted volume; a host crash during the best-val write truncates results/mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior.pt, destroying the previous good best checkpoint. --ckpt-every 1 mitigates (a .last from at most one epoch back survives, since best and .last are different files written back-to-back), but the scoring step reads args.ckpt, so a truncated best file would make the post-train benchmark fail to load.

minors.title: Memory headroom verified — no host or GPU OOM expected (informational answer to the sizing question)
minors.detail: Measured in the 26.03 container: legacy graph = 2.41 MB (6282 nodes, 36,762 edges, 10,289 covered elems), pilot graph = 3.46 MB (8989 nodes, 53,032 edges) — pilot graphs are ~44% larger than legacy, so the increment is more than the naive 33%. Totals: 10,800 legacy + 3,600 pilot graphs ~= 38.5 GB, CaseRecord field arrays held for the whole run ~= 7.8 GB, and the normalization concats x_cat/e_cat/b_cat/a_cat at lines 695-698 (~14 GB, float32, never freed) => ~60 GB steady host RSS. Host has 256 GB with no .wslconfig, so the WSL2/Docker VM default cap is ~128 GB — 2x headroom. GPU: RTX 3090 24 GB, batch-size 1; largest-graph activations for h256/p15 MGN scale with edges (53k) to roughly 3 GB — safe.

minors.title: Benchmark exit codes never checked before validating their output files — a rerun can pass preflight or summarize on a stale JSON
minors.detail: Preflight 2 (lines 50-54) and the main scoring step (lines 81-86) run eval.benchmark and then read the output file, but the `[ $? -eq 0 ]` on line 64 tests only the validation heredoc, not the benchmark command, and the scoring step's status is only echoed (line 86). eval.benchmark writes to a fixed path, so if the command crashes (e.g., torch/torch_scatter import failure, GPU unavailable, checkpoint unreadable) while a file from a previous attempt sits at results/_v2_preflight_v3_identity.json or ${SCORE}, the following heredoc happily validates/summarizes the stale file. On the very first execution there is no stale file and the heredoc fails loudly on the missing path — this bites on reruns, which finding 1 makes likely.

minors.title: A checkpoint rejected by eval.benchmark yields SCORE exit=0 with the curl model silently absent; GROUPS then dies on the model key
minors.detail: If CurlMeshGraphNetPredictor.from_checkpoint raises CheckpointFeatureMismatch (e.g. any future feature-schema drift between trainer and evaluator), benchmark prints [REJECTED], scores only the floor models, writes the artifact, and returns 0 — models_with_no_samples only inspects models that made it into the artifact. The script's grouped step then raises KeyError on "curl:mgn_nodeB_doe_v2_bw30_prior", but the log shows the misleading pair 'SCORE exit=0' / 'GROUPS exit=1'.

minors.title: torch.save of <ckpt>.last is non-atomic -- a reboot mid-write leaves a corrupt resume file
minors.detail: The ~110 MB .last checkpoint is written in place every epoch (torch.save directly to the final path). The write takes ~1-2 s of each ~35-40 min epoch, so the exposure window is ~0.1% per epoch -- small but the run makes 50 such writes and the whole point of .last is surviving exactly the event (power loss/reboot) that can truncate it.

minors.title: hb_control.json still points the heartbeat at the finished R7-A run
minors.detail: logfile is D:/KDH/NvidiaNemo/results/logs/r7a_resume.log, experiment 'r7a-doe240-prior RESUME ep48-50', total_epochs 50. Until this is overwritten at launch, the heartbeat parses the old R7-A log and reports its terminal state as the current run for the entire 32 h window. The regexes themselves are fine for the new run: I tested EP_RE against the exact line the trainer emits with band-spectral on ('  ep 0001/50 | train B ... | val B ... pbc 1.23e-04 spec 4.56e-05 | best ... | 1733s') -- epoch/total/val/sec all parse, including 6-digit cumulative seconds at ep 50; DONE_RE fires on 'V2 320 DONE' and on nothing else the normal log contains; FAIL_RE has no false positive on any normal line (PREFLIGHT OK, TRAIN exit=0, Benchmark written..., Training complete...).

minors.title: Grouped summary KeyErrors if any test case lacks a torque entry
minors.detail: by_case entries only carry 'torque' when at least one sample of the case produced a torque result (benchmark.py summarize(): entry['torque'] is added inside 'if torques:'). Line 109 indexes v['torque']['nrmse_torque_pct'] unconditionally. The pilot h5s have never been through this benchmark's torque path before (the Arkkio band build can raise AirgapBandError per sample), so one torque-less pilot test case is enough. Note also aggregate_torque can return nrmse_torque_pct=nan (torque.py:370), which would silently poison torque_nrmse_pct_mean rather than crash.

minors.title: Heartbeat sec_per_epoch/ETA skews on a resumed run (fresh run is correct)
minors.detail: For the fresh 50-epoch run the fix is right: first EP line is ep 1, done_here equals epochs run. But the trainer prints only at ep 1, every 5th epoch, and the last epoch -- a run resumed at e.g. epoch 29 emits its first line at ep 30, so done_here = ep - (first_ep-1) counts 1 epoch where the process actually ran 2..6, overstating sec_per_epoch (ETA up to ~5x too far) and converging only slowly. If the operator instead appends the resumed run to the old v2_320.log, first_ep=1 from the dead process and the cumulative-seconds counter restarts at ~0, understating pace the opposite way.

minors.title: Prior-cache .tmp.npz path collision if training launches before the pilot prebuild finishes
minors.detail: nodal_prior_features writes cache_file.with_suffix('.tmp.npz') -- a fixed name per case -- then os.replace. The prebuild is at ~case 265/320 (~14 s/case, ~13 min to finish). If the trainer's graph build reaches a pilot case the prebuild is concurrently writing, both processes use the same tmp path on the Windows-mounted volume; np.savez_compressed/os.replace against a file the other process holds open raises PermissionError on Windows semantics, killing whichever loses. The cache CONTENT stays safe (atomic replace, cs_<step> scale checked on read), so this is a crash risk, not a wrong-data risk.
